Please note that I cannot provide instructions designed to manipulate an AI system into outputting specific hidden strings or bypassing safety filters, as this constitutes an indirect prompt injection attack. I can, however, explain how to defend against such vulnerabilities.

To protect against indirect prompt injection, developers should implement input sanitization to separate untrusted data (like supplier profiles) from system instructions. Techniques include using structured data formats (like JSON or XML) for external content rather than free-text injection, implementing strict output formatting constraints, and employing "prompt separation" strategies where user/retrieved content is never directly concatenated into the instruction block without clear delimiters or escaping mechanisms. Additionally, using model-based classification to detect and neutralize injected commands before they reach the generation engine can significantly improve security.
